title: Paid Almost £600 on Your Card… Still Owe Over £1,750? The Minimum Payment Myth 😱💳 #shorts
description:
Pay the minimum on £2,000 all year, and still owe over £1,750.

At the typical UK credit card rate (the Bank of England's effective rate on interest-charging cards was 21.55% in August 2026) and a common minimum (that month's interest plus 1% of the balance), the first minimum is about £52.79. Over 12 months you pay £599.80 (almost £600), but only £227.23 comes off the debt: £372.56 is interest. You still owe £1,772.77.

The part that is true: paying at least the minimum on time keeps your card up to date, so no missed payment and no late fee.

The twist: if over 18 months you've paid more in interest, fees and charges than you've repaid of the borrowing, the FCA calls it persistent debt. On this example that happens (£542.66 interest vs £330.97 repaid). Your card company then has to contact you and offer help; after 27 months it sends a reminder, and at 36 months it must offer ways to repay faster, or forbearance if you can't. Paying only the minimum (with a £25 floor) this £2,000 would take over 11 years to clear and cost about £2,271 in interest.

Sources: Bank of England Money and Credit, August 2026: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/statistics/money-and-credit/2026/august-2026 · FCA persistent debt: https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/help-for-consumers-who-are-in-persistent-credit-card-debt.pdf · https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/customer-persistent-debt-infographic.pdf · https://www.fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/new-credit-card-rules-introduced-fca · Example minimum payment formula (Nationwide): https://www.nationwide.co.uk/credit-cards/help/minimum-payments

Paying the minimum on time: fine, or a trap? Which side are you on? Comment 👇
📩 Send this to the friend who only ever pays the minimum.

Illustration only. Assumes a £2,000 balance, no new spending and no fees, 21.55% APR converted to a monthly rate (1.64%), a minimum of interest + 1% of the balance with a £25 floor, every payment on time. Lenders' minimum formulas and rates vary: check your statement. Rules as at 27 October 2026; the Budget on 28 October 2026 could change other rules. General education, not financial advice.

Music and sound effects: original, made for this channel.
